title: No. 1 Open Weight Legal AI Debuts in Zai's First Professional Model
summary:
Zai's new GLM-Legal model scored 19.2% on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, more than double the 8.3% result of the full-size GLM 5.3 and triple the 6.7% of GLM 5.3 Flash. Built on the Flash architecture, the system is now the top open weight model on both LegalBench and Harvey's benchmark, meeting 92.5% of the individual criteria for complex legal assignments involving spreadsheets and presentations. It was designed to handle professional workloads such as evidence analysis, contract review, and compliance.

The model costs $0.15 per Harvey's task, roughly 70 times less than the $10.55 required for Gemini 4 Argon. Performance on LegalBench increased by 2.3 percentage points, with a 5 point jump in interpretation tasks, partly due to lower token usage per answer. However, GLM-Legal trailed GLM 5.3 Flash by 4 points on the LegalResearchBench because it searched case law only 6 times per question compared to 16 times for the base model.

selectedTweets.text:
Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark tests full legal assignments using documents, spreadsheets, and presentations. On this benchmark, it scored 19.2%, about 3x higher than the regular GLM 5.3 Flash (6.7%) and more than double the full-size GLM 5.3 (8.3%).

GLM 5.3 Flash Legal met 92.5% of the individual criteria, up from 82.2% for GLM 5.3 Flash. It scored higher because it missed fewer requirements and fully finished so many more tasks.

It scores #6 overall and at about $0.15 per task, it costs roughly 70 times less than Gemini 4 Argon (#5), which costs about $10.55 per task.

selectedTweets.bestBit: improved 2.3pp from GLM 5.3 Flash and the biggest gain came in interpretation tasks, which rose 5pts.
selectedTweets.text:
LegalBench tests short non-agentic legal reasoning questions. 5.3 Flash Legal improved 2.3pp from GLM 5.3 Flash and the biggest gain came in interpretation tasks, which rose 5pts. It is now the top open-weight model on LegalBench, just ahead of Kimi K3.

It also costs half as much per question as GLM 5.3 Flash. Per-token pricing is identical, so the savings come from the legal version using fewer tokens to answer.

selectedTweets.bestBit: searched case law much less frequently, about 6 times per question, compared with 16 for GLM 5.3 Flash.
selectedTweets.text:
Despite the increases on HLAB and Legal Bench, we saw a decrease on LegalResearchBench, which tests legal research using case-law search and the web.

Although it scored 4 points behind GLM 5.3 Flash, its answers were mostly correct, earning 86.1% of rubric points. However, it missed a required point more often. It also searched case law much less frequently, about 6 times per question, compared with 16 for GLM 5.3 Flash.
